raw_response:
I farm only 5 mu, so I cannot take big risks. What feeds my family is the wheat-maize rotation, same as most people here. I only went to primary school, so I do it mostly by what I have seen over the years and what the neighbors around me do. Last years when wheat looked weak, the people who topdressed once more at jointing got better grain, so for wheat I will still use fertilizer in two splits, but not too heavy because fertilizer and pumping water both cost money. For maize, the land comes out of wheat and the time is tight, so I will keep it simple: harvest wheat, quickly clear the field, shallow rotary once, then sow hybrid maize right away. I have a well, so if it turns dry I will irrigate, but I will not water too many times because electricity and pumping add up. Some people in my house work outside, so I want a plan that family labor can handle without hiring much help. I would rather spend a little on seed and fertilizer than let the crop fall short, but I still need to keep some cash in hand.
